scope: OpenWrt configuration backup and restore: keep native sysupgrade -b/-r behavior, retain integrity and transfer checks, remove the app-only directory and symlink-target restrictions.
root_cause: The application added its own restore policy on top of the native archive: only etc/ and root/ top-level entries, symlink targets inside that set (plus an nginx/collectd allowlist), and a remote check that rejected existing symlink parents. OpenWrt itself backs up every path in /etc/sysupgrade.conf and /lib/upgrade/keep.d, including arbitrary directories and symlinks, and restores with tar -C / -xzf. A backup generated by the router could therefore be refused by the application.
behavior: Export and restore now run the same inspect_archive check; there is no export-only relaxed mode and no restore-only extra policy.
Removed the top-level etc/root restriction, the symlink-target range restriction, the nginx/collectd target allowlist, and the parent_guard remote symlink-parent check.

Kept container safety: regular file and size limit, gzip/tar validity, bounded expanded size and entry count, normalized relative member names without traversal, duplicate rejection, special-file rejection, internal file/symlink parent conflict rejection, and an etc/config presence check.
Kept SHA256 verification of the router-generated archive, the download, the frozen pre-restore snapshot, and the uploaded archive; kept the router-side tar listing comparison before any write.
Kept the existing restore confirmation covering trusted-source responsibility and possible changes to the management address, login password and Wi-Fi.
No new router command was introduced: still sysupgrade -b, sysupgrade -r, tar -tzf, sha256sum and df.

official_verification.method: Read the official OpenWrt base-files sysupgrade script for the oldest and current supported series; SHA256 was computed on every downloaded file.
findings: sysupgrade -b creates a gzip-compressed tar from the explicit file list built from /etc/sysupgrade.conf and /lib/upgrade/keep.d; list_backup_files selects both -type f and -type l, so custom directories and symlinks are legitimate.
sysupgrade -r restores with tar -C / -xzf without an etc/root prefix filter.
19.07, 23.05 and the 25.12 branch use the same -b/-r options and restore command.

real_archive_preflight.file: config backup supplied by the user (2026-11-18)
real_archive_preflight.result: passed the current inspection and the offline preview path; no restore command was sent to any router

tests.command: python -m unittest tests.test_router_backup tests.test_maintenance_ui tests.test_maintenance_choices tests.test_optional_restore_backup tests.test_management_log_audit tests.test_common_settings_second_audit tests.test_router_policy
coverage: custom top-level directory and /root file accepted
absolute and parent-relative symlink targets accepted
archive-internal symlink parent conflict still rejected
path traversal, absolute member, duplicate member and special files still rejected
corrupt archive, oversized archive and cancellation rejected
download corruption preserves the existing local file
custom-path backup can be previewed and restored end to end in the offline device adapter
native tar listing mismatch blocks restore before writes

limitations: No restore was executed on a real router; only read-only local inspection and the offline command adapter were used.
Hardlinks and special files remain rejected deliberately; native sysupgrade normally backs up regular files and symlinks only.
The user-supplied archive is only one device sample; other firmware-specific paths were covered by synthetic archives in tests.
